title: Leaves Don't Turn Orange in Fall 🍂 (Here's Why)
description:
Leaves don't turn orange in fall. The orange was in there all summer 🍂
Green chlorophyll covers it up. When days get shorter and cooler, the leaf stops making chlorophyll, the green fades and the hidden yellow and orange show. Reds are made new in fall.

description:

title: Why Flamingos Are Pink 🦩 (They're Born Grey)
description:
Flamingos are born GREY 🩶 The pink is 100% from their food.
Algae make natural pigments called carotenoids → brine shrimp eat the algae → flamingos eat the shrimp and turn it into pink feathers, legs and beaks.
Stop eating it and the pink fades. That's why zoos add pigment to their food 🦩
Sweetest part: parents feed their chick "crop milk" and go pale doing it.
Which animal should we explain next? 👇
Sources: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance; Smithsonian Magazine.

title: One Galaxy, THREE Giant Black Holes 🕳️
description:
One galaxy. THREE giant black holes 🕳️ Astronomers used the James Webb telescope to spot them in a galaxy we see as it was over 12 billion years ago, and two of them may soon merge. Black holes in plain English: 1) gravity so strong nothing escapes, 2) "active" ones glow because they're eating gas, 3) Webb split the light into colors to find them. The authors call it evidence, not the final word.
Would you want a Part 2 on what happens when black holes merge? Comment "MERGE" 👇 and subscribe for more.

title: Octopuses Have 3 Hearts and Blue Blood 🐙
description:
An octopus has THREE hearts 💙 and blue blood.
2 hearts push blood through the gills, 1 sends it to the body, and that main one stops beating when it swims (so they'd rather crawl 😮‍💨).
Its blood uses copper-based hemocyanin instead of iron, so it's blue. It works better in cold, low-oxygen water but it's thick, so it needs the extra pumps.

title: Why a Damaged QR Code Still Scans 📱
description:
This black-and-white square can be partly destroyed and your phone STILL reads it 📱 The secret: three corner squares tell your phone where the code is, and hidden "backup" math (Reed-Solomon codes) repairs missing pieces. The strongest setting can fix up to roughly 30% damage. (Exact limits vary by level.)

Did you know QR codes were invented in 1994 to track car parts? 👇 Subscribe for more.

title: Your Microwave Does NOT Cook From the Inside Out 🔥
description:
Your microwave does NOT cook food from the inside out 🔥 It's a myth. The waves make water molecules spin, spinning makes friction, friction makes heat, but the waves only reach about 1 cm into most foods. The middle warms up later as heat spreads. (Depth varies by food.)

Tip: stir it and let it sit a minute. Did you know this? 👇 Subscribe for more.

title: Why You Get Dizzy After Spinning 🌀
description:
Why you get dizzy after spinning 🌀 Inside your inner ear are 3 tiny loops filled with fluid. When you stop, the fluid keeps moving for a moment (like tea in a cup), so your ears say "spinning!" while your eyes say "still." That mismatch is the dizzy feeling.

Dancers and skaters use "spotting" (eyes on one spot, head snaps around late). Dizziness has many causes, this is just the spinning kind.

title: Noise-Cancelling Headphones Fight Sound With Sound 🎧
description:
Noise-cancelling headphones don't just BLOCK sound. They fight it with MORE sound 🎧 Tiny mics listen, a chip flips the wave upside down, and when the two meet your ear, up cancels down. It works best on steady hums (airplane engines) and struggles with sudden sounds like voices.
